name: Eventual

modes.label: Daft open-source self-hosted engine
modes.note: Daft software is free/open source and runs on the customer's laptop, Kubernetes or Ray infrastructure. CPU, GPU, RAM, storage, model/API and network costs are charged by those external providers; no Eventual per-resource tariff is published.

modes.label: Eventual robotics data platform
modes.note: Early-access/contact-only commercial platform for scenario search/mining and training-set curation over robot fleet video and telemetry. No public tariff, infrastructure model, concurrency, quota or retention terms.

plans.name: Eventual commercial platform
plans.note: Contact/demo only; no public pricing page.

features.gpu_scheduling: Daft accepts fractional GPU values up to 1.0 and integer counts above 1, with max_concurrency for sharing; hardware/type/price come from the customer's infrastructure.

caveats: Public open-source multimodal engine and cloud/BYOC offering; arbitrary Python UDFs may fit batch compute, but no captured per-vCPU tariff. Not a general interactive sandbox. Customer infrastructure and platform price must be distinguished.
Null values mean unknown, not free/unlimited. No model-token cost, tax or unverified ancillary charge included.
Native browser/device/task/credit prices with unknown CPU/RAM are deliberately non-priceable. Check regime before interpreting any partial resource estimate.

harness_api.quote: Eventual is the commercial platform robotics teams use to mine scenarios and curate training sets on robot fleet data.
harness_api.note: Category mismatch rather than an explicit 'not supported' statement: Eventual is a robotics scenario-mining/data-curation platform and Daft is a Python/SQL dataframe engine; neither offers a sandbox or any API to drive Claude Code/Codex/etc. Daft 'AI functions' (prompt/embed/classify) call model providers per row; that is batch inference, not an agent harness.
